metadata.summary: The BraTS 2024 challenge provides multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) scans with ground truth annotations for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification across multiple sub-challenges: post-treatment glioma (≈2,200 patients), pre-treatment glioma (≈1,250 training cases plus additional), pediatric tumors (≈2,490), meningioma (≈650), brain metastases (≈460), and an Africa subset (≈750). Includes an unseen test set of over 4,000 patients and a histopathology extension with 280,000 tiles.
metadata.purpose: To support benchmarking of AI models for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification.

papers.title: BraTS 2024: Diverse tasks for brain tumor segmentation, survival prediction, and molecular marker classification

ethics.privacy_measures: De-identification of all patient data prior to release.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: The following LLM fields were auto-dropped for violating schema constraints and reverted to baseline; pending manual review: medical_fields[list-items], tasks_and_use/intended_tasks[list-items]

known_limitations: Geographic representation limited despite Africa subset; majority of data likely from high-resource settings.
No reported age, sex, or ethnicity distributions — limits bias assessment.
Histopathology extension (280,000 tiles) lacks patient-level linkage or clinical metadata.
Test set is unseen and unannotated — prevents direct performance validation on held-out population.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Data de-identified; no mention of synthetic data or augmentation applied to released dataset.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: Overrepresentation of glioma; underrepresentation of non-glioma adult brain tumors; Africa subset small relative to global burden.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Meningioma (≈650) and brain metastases (≈460) are substantially smaller than pediatric (≈2,490) and glioma cohorts.
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Generalizability limited to populations and imaging protocols represented across participating international sites; unknown temporal drift due to unspecified collection period.
bias_and_limitations.subgroup_coverage: Covers pediatric, African-origin, and treatment-stage (pre-/post-) subgroups; no coverage reported for pregnancy, elderly-specific, or critical-care subgroups.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic variables (age, sex, ethnicity) not reported; clinical metadata (e.g., treatment history, outcomes beyond survival) incomplete for some subsets.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Real-time clinical deployment; direct diagnostic use without regulatory validation.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Cases selected to represent diverse brain tumor types (glioma pre-/post-treatment, pediatric, meningioma, metastases) and geographic diversity (including Africa subset).
data_origin.sampling_strategy: Multi-site clinical collection; stratified by tumor type and clinical setting (e.g., pre- vs. post-treatment); Africa subset explicitly included to improve geographic representation.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from multiple international clinical sites; no description of harmonization or recoding of demographic attributes provided in source text.

population.target_population: Patients with brain tumors including glioma (pre- and post-treatment), pediatric brain tumors, meningioma, brain metastases, and African-origin cases.
population.inclusion_criteria: Clinical diagnosis of specified brain tumor types; availability of multi-parametric MRI and associated annotations.
population.missing_groups: No explicit reporting of underrepresented groups beyond the stated effort to include Africa subset; sex, age, and ethnicity distributions not reported.

annotation.annotation_method: Expert manual or semi-automatic annotation by radiologists/neuro-oncologists; ground truth provided per sub-challenge task.

annotators.qualifications: Clinical experts in neuro-oncology and neuroradiology

annotation.labeling_provenance: Ground truth annotations generated by expert consensus or verified by clinical specialists per sub-challenge.
